body.heading: The cycle, not the grind
paragraphs: Muscles are not built during exercise; they are built during the recovery afterwards. The same pattern shows up in learning and creative work: effort stresses the system, and rest is when the system adapts and consolidates.
Treating rest as laziness breaks the cycle in the middle. People who push without pause do not usually get more done over a season — they get tired, make more errors, and often stop altogether.

body.heading: Rest on purpose
paragraphs: Real rest is more than collapsing with a phone. It might be sleep, a walk without headphones, an undemanding hobby, or simply an evening with nothing scheduled. The test is whether you return with something restored.
If you are picking yourself up after a setback, build the rest in first and the retry second. Trying again works much better on a recovered mind than on an exhausted one.

takeaway: Plan the rest as seriously as the retry — they are one cycle.
